column2: Light Weight Fighters are intended to be the 'militia' of the air force.Cheap and fast to build, they are not however as good as your regular interceptors.
column5: Los cazas ligeros representan la 'milicia' de la fuerza aérea. Son económicos y rápidos de fabricar, aunque su rendimiento combativo es inferior al de los interceptores convencionales.

column2: A multiple independently targetable reentry vehicle (MIRV) is a ballistic missile payload containing several warheads, each capable of hitting one of a group of targets.
column5: Un vehículo de reentrada múltiple independiente (MIRV) es una carga de misil balístico con varias ojivas nucleares, cada una orientada a batir un blanco distinto de forma simultánea.

column2: Helicopter CAG are specialized in ASW duties, they can only operate from a helicopter or light carrier.
column5: Los grupos aéreos embarcados de helicópteros se especializan en misiones antisubmarinas (GAS) y solo pueden operar desde portahelicópteros o portaaviones ligeros.

column2: The Armored Box Launcher (ABL) is a four-round protected launch container for a Cruise Missile.
column5: El lanzador blindado de caja (ABL) es un contenedor de lanzamiento protegido de cuatro celdas diseñado para disparar misiles de crucero de largo alcance.

column2: In V/STOL the VTOL aircraft moves horizontally along the runway before taking off using vertical thrust. This gives aerodynamic lift as well as thrust lift and permits taking off with heavier loads and is more efficient.
column5: En un despegue V/STOL, el aparato carretea en horizontal antes de emplear el empuje vectorial vertical, logrando sustentación aerodinámica para despegar con mayor carga útil de armas.

column2: An airborne early warning and control (AEW&C) system is an airborne radar system designed to detect aircraft, ships and vehicles at long ranges and control and command the battle space in an air engagement by directing fighter and attack aircraft strikes. AEW&C units are also used to carry out surveillance, including over ground targets and frequently perform C2BM (command and control, battle management) functions similar to an Airport Traffic Controller given military command over other forces. Used at a high altitude, the radars on the aircraft allow the operators to distinguish between friendly and hostile aircraft hundreds of miles away.
column5: Un sistema de alerta temprana y control aerotransportado (AWACS/AEW&C) utiliza un radar de largo alcance a gran altitud para vigilar y dirigir formaciones aéreas amigas hacia sus blancos con precisión.

column2: Usually, the aircraft providing the fuel is specially designed for the task, although refueling pods can be fitted to existing aircraft designs if the "probe-and-drogue" system is to be used (see later). The cost of the refueling equipment on both tanker and receiver aircraft and the specialized aircraft handling of the aircraft to be refueled (very close "line astern" formation flying) has resulted in the activity only being used in military operations. There is no known regular civilian in-flight refueling activity.
column5: Los aviones nodriza de reabastecimiento en vuelo extienden enormemente el radio operativo de cazas y bombarderos mediante mangueras y receptáculos de combustible en el aire.

column2: A CAG for the Heavy Aviation Cruisers, what did you expect?
column5: Grupo aéreo embarcado (GAE) dotado de aviones y helicópteros especialmente adaptados a las cubiertas de vuelo de cruceros pesados portaeronaves.

column2: Your naval commandos can only operate from a light carrier and they greatly increase the shore bombardment and land detection values of that carrier in question.
column5: Los comandos navales operan desde portaaviones ligeros para realizar incursiones en costas hostiles, mejorando sustancialmente el bombardeo litoral y la detección costera.

column2: A close-in weapon system (CIWS), often pronounced sea-whiz, is a naval shipboard point-defense weapon for detecting and destroying short range incoming anti-ship missiles and enemy aircraft which have penetrated the outer defenses.
column5: Un sistema de armas de proximidad (CIWS) es un montaje automático de tiro rápido y radar autónomo para neutralizar misiles antibuque y aeronaves a muy corta distancia.

column2: Like a regular corvette, but this time, with missiles instead of guns granting them higher seattack values but lowe ASW values.
column5: Una corbeta rápida armada con baterías de misiles antibuque guiados, lo que le otorga gran pegada de ataque de superficie a cambio de una capacidad antisubmarina reducida.

column2: A corvette (sometimes corvet) is a small, maneuverable, lightly armed warship, originally smaller than a frigate (2,000+ tons) and larger than a coastal patrol craft or fast attack craft (500 or fewer tons),[1] although many recent designs resemble frigates in size and role. During the Age of Sail, corvettes were smaller than frigates and larger than sloops-of-war, usually with a single gun deck.
column5: Un buque de guerra pequeño, ligero y maniobrable, optimizado para misiones de patrulla costera, detección acústica y lucha antisubmarina en aguas litorales.

column2: Anti-tank guns are guns designed to destroy armored vehicles from defensive positions. In order to penetrate vehicle armor they fire smaller caliber shells from longer-barreled guns to achieve higher muzzle velocity than field artillery weapons, many of which are howitzers. The higher velocity, flatter trajectory ballistics provide terminal kinetic energy to penetrate the moving/static target's armor at a given range and contact's angle. Any field artillery cannon with barrel length 15 to 25 times longer than its caliber was able also to fire anti-tank ammunition.
column5: Piezas de artillería de tiro tenso y alta velocidad inicial diseñadas específicamente para batir y penetrar el blindaje frontal y lateral de tanques enemigos en posiciones defensivas.

column2: Ultra Big Tanks. They make boo-boo to your enemies.
column5: Blindados monstruosos de proporciones gigantescas. Concebidos como acorazados terrestres fuertemente artillados, infligen una devastación catastrófica en las líneas defensivas enemigas.

column2: Special forces, or special operations forces are military units highly-trained to perform unconventional, often high-risk missions. Special forces, as they would now be recognised, emerged in the early 20th century, with a significant growth in the field during the Second World War.
column5: Destacamentos de élite con adiestramiento intensivo para misiones encubiertas de sabotaje, reconocimiento estratégico e infiltración tras las líneas enemigas.
Destructor de gran desplazamiento con amplios sensores sónicos y armas de ataque a submarinos, optimizado para escoltar convoyes marítimos y agrupaciones navales de gran valor.

column2: A guided missile destroyer is a destroyer designed to launch guided missiles. Many are also equipped to carry out anti-submarine, anti-air, and anti-surface operations. The NATO standard designation for these vessels is DDG. Nations vary in their use of destroyer D designation their hull pennant numbering, either prefixing, or dropping it altogether.
column5: Destructor moderno dotado de celdas de lanzamiento para misiles guiados de defensa aérea, superficie y guerra submarina, sirviendo como núcleo de escolta de la flota.

column2: In modern navies, frigates are used to protect other warships and merchant-marine ships, especially as anti-submarine warfare (ASW) combatants for amphibious expeditionary forces, underway replenishment groups, and merchant convoys. Ship classes dubbed "frigates" have also more closely resembled corvettes, destroyers, cruisers and even battleships.
column5: Buques de escolta oceánica diseñados principalmente para la protección de convoyes mercantes y grupos anfibios frente a amenazas submarinas y ataques aéreos ligeros.

column2: A ballistic missile submarine is a submarine equipped to launch ballistic missiles (SLBMs). The world's first ballistic missile submarine was a Soviet converted Zulu class submarine equipped with a single ballistic missile launch tube in its sail. Today's ballistic missile submarines are larger than any other type of submarine, in order to accommodate SLBMs such as the Russian R-29 or the American Trident. Although some early models had to surface to launch their missiles, modern vessels typically launch while submerged at keel depths of usually less than 50 meters (164 feet).
column5: Sumergibles de propulsión nuclear equipados con silos verticales de misiles balísticos (SLBM), sirviendo como la plataforma submarina definitiva de disuasión nuclear.

column2: The main difference between conventional submarines and nuclear submarines is the power generation system. Nuclear submarines employ nuclear reactors for this task. They either generate electricity that powers electric motors connected to the propeller shaft or rely on the reactor heat to produce steam that drives steam turbines (cf. nuclear marine propulsion). Reactors used in submarines typically use highly enriched fuel (often greater than 20per cent) to enable them to deliver a large amount of power from a smaller reactor and operate longer between refuelings – which are difficult due to the reactor's position within the submarine's pressure hull.
column5: Submarinos de propulsión atómica capaces de alcanzar velocidades bajo el agua sin necesidad de emerger a la superficie, ideales para cazar flotas y submarinos rivales.

column2: The nuclear cruisers are designed to keep steaming for years between refuelings. They are not very different from their non nuclear counterparts except in their fuel consumption values.
column5: Cruceros dotados de propulsión por reactor atómico, lo que les permite sostener alta velocidad de crucero ilimitada en el mar durante años sin requerir combustible fósil.

column2: Air assault is the movement of ground-based military forces by vertical take-off and landing (VTOL) aircraft—such as the helicopter—to seize and hold key terrain which has not been fully secured, and to directly engage enemy forces.In addition to regular infantry training, air-assault units usually receive training in rappelling and air transportation, and their equipment is sometimes designed or field-modified to allow better transportation within aircraft.
column5: Unidades terrestres helitransportadas capacitadas para descender en helicópteros de maniobra y asegurar nudos tácticos clave de forma inmediata tras el frente.

column2: Air assault is the movement of ground-based military forces by vertical take-off and landing (VTOL) aircraft—such as the helicopter—to seize and hold key terrain which has not been fully secured, and to directly engage enemy forces.In addition to regular infantry training, air-assault units usually receive training in rappelling and air transportation, and their equipment is sometimes designed or field-modified to allow better transportation within aircraft.
column5: Grandes divisiones integradas por infantería de choque y flotas orgánicas de helicópteros de transporte y ataque para maniobras de embolsamiento relámpago.

column2: A gunship is an aircraft having laterally-mounted heavy armaments (i.e. firing to the side) to attack ground or sea targets. These gunships were configured to circle the target instead of performing strafing runs. Such aircraft have their armament on one side harmonized to fire at the apex of an imaginary cone formed by the aircraft and the ground when performing a pylon turn (banking turn).
column5: Aeronaves equipadas con cañones pesados en un costado de su fuselaje para trazar giros orbitales sobre el blanco y saturar posiciones enemigas de tierra con fuego continuo.

column2: Counter-insurgency aircraft are a specialised variety of military light attack aircraft, designed for light counter-insurgency, armed reconnaissance, air escort of ground forces, and ground support against 'low-intensity engagements', usually irregular groups of insurgents. They are usually armed with cannon and/or small-calibre rockets.
column5: Aviones de ataque ligero y hélice optimizados para misiones de patrulla armada, apoyo a convoyes y bombardeo de baja intensidad contra facciones guerrilleras o partisanos.

column2: An attack helicopter is a military helicopter with the primary role of an attack aircraft, with the capability of engaging targets on the ground, such as enemy infantry and armored vehicles. Due to their heavy armament they are sometimes called helicopter gunships.
column5: Aeronaves de alas rotatorias provistas de blindaje, ametralladoras rotativas y misiles guiados diseñadas para neutralizar columnas mecanizadas y tanques enemigos.

column2: Naval Helicopters are the true heirs to floatplanes. They are used to scout the surrounding naval area of operations in search of submarines and other potential threats to the ship or fleet integrity
column5: Helicópteros navales embarcados equipados con radar de superficie, torpedos acústicos y sonoboyas para localizar y batir submarinos en torno a la escuadra.

column2: Infantry will most likely make up the bulk of your army. They are relatively cheap to build and require no regular fuel supply to manoeuvre, but their lack of motorized transport means their speed of advance is limited. However, Infantry are able to occupy large areas of land, securing ground captured by other forces.
column5: La infantería conforma la médula espinal de cualquier ejército. No consume combustible de forma regular, es económica de reclutar y resulta idónea para guarnecer y ocupar terreno.

column2: Cavalry are able to move fairly rapidly over most types of terrain and do not require a supply of fuel to operate, but they are lightly armed when compared with Armoured units, and the automatic weapons of the time can inflict devastating casualties to both men and horses. That is not to say that Cavalry can't prove useful in some instances as a mobile reserve.
column5: La caballería se desplaza con agilidad sobre terrenos agrestes sin exigir combustible, pero carece del blindaje de los carros y es vulnerable al fuego de armas automáticas.

column2: Motorized Infantry make use of wheeled vehicles, such as trucks, to manoeuvre more rapidly than basic Infantry. But they are limited to roads and so their performance may suffer in provinces with low infrastructure levels.
column5: Infantería dotada de camiones y vehículos de ruedas para marchar a gran velocidad, aunque su rendimiento se reduce notablemente en regiones con malas infraestructuras.

column2: Mechanized Infantry are equipped with all-terrain vehicles, such as the halftrack, which does not limit them to roads as with Motorized Infantry and allows them to work well with armoured units. However, the specialist equipment they require means their cost is high.
column5: Infantería embarcada en transportes oruga o semiorugas blindados para maniobrar campo a través junto a las divisiones acorazadas con gran protección balística.

column2: Armoured units allow real projection of power on the battlefield. Their speed and firepower make them lethal against all but the best entrenched Infantry. However, as tanks become heavier, their speeds will reduce accordingly.  They also require a constant supply of fuel to remain in the field and if this vital supply is severed, the armoured unit will be almost useless.
column5: Los tanques ligeros ofrecen gran velocidad de maniobra y potencia para envolver infanterías desprotegidas, pero requieren un suministro constante e ininterrumpido de combustible.

column2: Armoured units allow real projection of power on the battlefield. Their speed and firepower make them lethal against all but the best entrenched Infantry. However, as tanks became heaver, their speeds would reduce accordingly.  They also required a constant supply of fuel to remain in the field, and if this vital supply was severed, the armoured unit would be next to useless.
column5: Puntas de lanza blindadas de alta potencia de choque y avance. Su pegada es destructiva frente a líneas enemigas, pero quedan inmovilizadas si se interrumpe su petróleo.

column2: Paratroopers are an elite branch of the Infantry, specifically trained to either parachute to the ground or be ferried to a battle in gliders. Their rapid deployment capability makes them ideal for use as a mobile reserve or for use in capturing a strategic asset behind enemy lines. However, they are handicapped by a lack of heavy equipment due to their mode of travel, and when they are in action it is advisable to move other units to their support.
column5: Fuerzas de élite lanzadas desde aviones en paracaídas para capturar nudos logísticos y cabezas de puente tras las líneas enemigas, aunque carecen de armas pesadas de apoyo.

column2: Marines are an elite branch of the Infantry, specifically trained for assaulting beaches and other naval operations. They make use of specialised equipment and tactics to give them an edge over regular Infantry in such an environment.
column5: Infantería de asalto naval altamente instruida para desembarcar en playas defendidas, cruzar vías fluviales y sostener cabezas de playa bajo fuego artillero costero.

column2: Mountain Troops are an elite branch of the Infantry, specifically trained for operations in mountainous terrain.  They make use of specialised equipment and tactics to give them an edge over regular Infantry in such an environment.
column5: Unidades especializadas con equipo ligero de escalada y armamento adaptado para combatir con ventaja táctica en cumbres montañosas y pasos nevados.

column2: Garrison Divisions are second line troops used to safeguard valuable objectives far from the front lines. They lack heavy equipment and transportation, making them immobile except for strategic redeployment. They have limited fighting capability but can be used to free more capable troops for frontline use.
column5: Tropas estáticas de retaguardia para defensa de puntos neurálgicos y represión de insurgentes. No pueden moverse a pie, requiriendo redespliegue estratégico por ferrocarril.

column2: Headquarters are the brains of your armed forces. They contain the staff that keeps your army running, such as logistics and planning staff. They give a bonus to the units fighting in the vicinity but it is advisable to guard them, as their own fighting ability is poor.
column5: Puestos de mando del Estado Mayor que elevan la eficacia combativa, coordinación y suministro de las divisiones cercanas, pero que precisan de constante escolta aliada.

column2: Close Air Support is the key to the blitzkrieg tactic. These planes have the ability to strike precisely at enemy units, enabling your ground forces to achieve a rapid breakthrough. They are slow, sturdy planes and this makes them an easy target for enemy fighters.
column5: Aeronaves de ataque a tierra y bombardeo en picado fundamentales en las guerras relámpago para desgastar columnas enemigas, pero vulnerables a cazas interceptores.

column2: Interceptors are short-range fighters designed to destroy enemy bombers. They have high speed and good manouverability to make them agile enough to evade the machine guns of the bombers, while having the firepower needed to disable a heavy, armoured bomber.  Against enemy fighters, they are less effective yet they still put up a good fight.
column5: Cazas de gran trepada y radio de acción corto diseñados para abatir oleadas de bombarderos enemigos antes de que alcancen sus objetivos fabriles o militares.

column2: Fighters are the backbone of any air force. They are used to achieve air superiority, engage enemy bombers and fighters. They are all-rounders, being able to fulfill any mission given to them, but excelling at none in particular.
column5: Cazas polivalentes con alcance equilibrado capaces de sostener patrullas de supremacía aérea, entablar combate cerrado con cazas y batir aparatos de bombardeo.

column2: Escort Fighters are long-range fighters, designed to escort bombers and keep enemy interceptors from the bombers. They are drilled in tactics to achieve this mission and receive a bonus when escorting bombers. In Air Superiority missions, they are less effective.
column5: Cazas con depósitos suplementarios de combustible adaptados para acompañar y proteger las formaciones de bombarderos estratégicos en incursiones de profundidad.

column2: Strategic Bombers are the heaviest type of aircraft, designed to deliver a large payload of bombs to enemy provinces, with the aim of crippling his industry and infrastructure. However, the Strategic Bomber is slow despite its long range, which can make it vulnerable to attack by fighters.
column5: Aparatos cuatrimotores de largo alcance orientados a soltar grandes cargas de bombas explosivas e incendiarias sobre fábricas, nudos ferroviarios y ciudades enemigas.

column2: Tactical Bombers are medium-sized aircraft, larger than Fighters, yet smaller than Strategic Bombers, which are used primarily for delivering attacks against enemy ground units such as Armour and Infantry.  Although they have a limited dog-fighting capability, they can be easily outmatched by Fighters in air combat.
column5: Bombarderos bimotores versátiles capaces de destruir divisiones terrestres, retrasar refuerzos en carreteras o destruir instalaciones industriales con notable precisión.

column2: Transport Planes are designed to ferry men and materials over long distances quickly. Paratroops need Transport Planes in order to make a paradrop.
column5: Grandes aviones de transporte logístico necesarios para abastecer tropas aisladas por vía aérea y lanzar divisiones completas de paracaidistas en asaltos verticales.

column2: The Battleship is the Queen of the Sea. It is a massive floating gun platform, designed primarily to engage enemy capital ships at long range and send them to the bottom of the ocean. However, they are now vulnerable to air or submarine torpedo attacks, and the advent of the Aircraft Carrier has started to number their days.
column5: Grandes navíos artilleros dotados de coraza maciza y cañones de grueso calibre para destruir buques de línea o bombardear las defensas de la costa.

column2: Light Cruisers are little more than large destroyers. They are usually lightly armored to give good speed and range. They are normally used in an escort role for capital ships like battleships or carriers, granting protection mainly from enemy air attacks, but also from enemy submarines.
column5: Buques de superficie ágiles que combinan velocidad con baterías antiaéreas de tiro rápido, sirviendo como pantalla de escolta antiaérea y antisubmarina de los buques capitales.

column2: Heavy Cruisers are larger and more heavily armored than their lighter counterparts. They have larger main guns, giving them the ability to bombard enemy units on land. They are effective against enemy surface ships, especially destroyers and light cruisers, but are susceptible to air and submarine attacks.
column5: Cruceros de protección reforzada armados con cañones de mediano calibre, idóneos para batir flotillas de destructores enemigos y apoyar invasiones en litorales costeros.

column2: Battlecruisers are very heavy cruisers that combine large main guns and good armor with reasonable speed and a good range. They are mainly used against enemy shipping lanes, able to outrun enemy battleships and able to outfight convoy escorts.
column5: Buques que aúnan el poder artillero de los acorazados con la velocidad de un crucero ligero, diseñados para cazar convoyes comerciales y huir de los acorazados pesados.

column2: The Destroyer is the smallest and the fastest of the surface ships. It is lightly armed in comparison with the battleship, but its speed and maneuverability allow it to provide a good first line of defence away from the main capital ships of a fleet, and its light guns are useful for engaging aircraft. Destroyers are usually combined in groups and used for convoy escort and anti-submarine duties.
column5: Navíos ligeros y veloces equipados con cargas de profundidad, hidrófonos y torpedos -  son indispensables para la defensa de convoyes y la cacería de submarinos.

column2: The Aircraft Carrier is rapidly becoming the most important naval vessel. Its ability to project power through the aircraft it carries makes it dangerous to other capital ships and land forces. However, the ship itself is only lightly armed and must rely on other naval units, as well as its own aircraft, to afford it protection.
column5: El eje supremo del combate marítimo moderno. Proyecta su pegada aérea a centenares de kilómetros contra flotas enemigas, requiriendo escolta de destructores y cruceros.

column2: The Submarine is designed to travel underwater allowing it to operate clandestinely against other naval units. Its main armament consists of torpedoes which are deadly against all other types of vessel, be they Carrier, Battleship, Naval Transport or another Submarine. However, the Submarine can be handicapped by a short range and new technologies to improve them can be expensive.
column5: Sumergibles de ataque sigiloso armados con torpedos, idóneos para asfixiar las rutas mercantes del enemigo o emboscar formaciones navales desprevenidas en alta mar.

column2: Naval Transports are used for moving supplies and resources around the world. They can also be used to ferry land units across stretches of water. They are completely unarmed and, unless well protected, will be vulnerable to attack by other naval units or aircraft.
column5: Buques desarmados de transporte indispensables para realizar desembarcos anfibios de divisiones terrestres y sostener rutas oceánicas de suministros a ultramar.

column2: Militia are a cheap and rapidly formed Infantry unit. Their hurried training and poor equipment mean they are of little use in combat, although they can be useful for controlling territory and as a last line of defence when no other units are available.
column5: Tropas irregulares de muy rápido reclutamiento y escasa potencia de fuego, empleadas para controlar territorio o defender desesperadamente regiones secundarias.

column2: The Naval Bomber is designed for use over water and make accurate tactical strikes against enemy surface vessels using torpedoes or armour-piercing bombs.  They have a limited dog-fighting capability, which makes them vulnerable if intercepted by fighters.
column5: Aviones de patrulla marítima provistos de torpedos y bombas antibuque para patrullar zonas marítimas y hundir formaciones navales o convoyes desprotegidos.

column2: The Flying Bomb (e.g. the German V1) is a pilotless aircraft powered by an early jet engine, designed to deliver a payload of explosives to an area target. It is slower than a rocket or missile, which means that it can be intercepted and shot down by enemy fighters.
column5: Misiles de crucero primitivos sin tripulación propulsados por pulsorreactores para bombardear ciudades enemigas, interceptables por artillería antiaérea o cazas veloces.

column2: The Rocket or Ballistic Missile (e.g. the German V2) is designed to deliver a payload of explosives to a distant target. Its high speed makes it almost impossible to intercept but it is an expensive way of destroying the enemy with conventional explosives.  Nuclear weapons are needed to give it more than psychological effect.
column5: Misiles balísticos guiados por motores de cohete de gran altitud. Su velocidad terminal hipersónica los vuelve prácticamente imposibles de interceptar con cazas.

column2: The Escort Carrier became an important naval vessel later in the war. column2: The Panzer-Lehr-Division, commonly known as Panzer Lehr, was a German armored division during World War II, one of the most elite units in the entire German Wehrmacht. It was formed in 1943 from various units of elite training and demonstration troops (Lehr = "teach") stationed in Germany, to provide additional armored strength for resisting the anticipated Allied invasion of western Europe. Its great weakness was that it concentrated the cream of Germany's tank commanders/instructors in a single unit. Due to its elite status it was lavishly equipped in comparison to the ordinary Panzer divisions, though on several occasions it fought almost to destruction, in particular during Operation Cobra.

The Brandenburgers was used as a commando unit during the first years of the war. Initially the unit consisted mainly of former German expatriates fluent in other languages.

column2: The Reichssicherheitsdienst (RSD) was an SS security force of Nazi Germany. Originally the personal bodyguards of Adolf Hitler, it later provided men for the protection of other high-ranking leaders of the Nazi regime. The group, although similar in name, was completely separate from the Sicherheitsdienst (SD) which was the formal intelligence service for the SS and entire Nazi Party.

column2: Schwerer Gustav and Dora were the names of two German 80 cm K (E) ultra-heavy railway guns. The twin guns weighed nearly 1,350 tonnes, and could fire shells weighing seven tonnes to a range of 47 kilometers (29 mi). The guns were designed in preparation for the Battle of France, but were not ready for action when the battle began, and in any case the Wehrmacht's Blitzkrieg offensive through Belgium rapidly outflanked and isolated the Maginot Line's World War I-era static defenses, forcing them to surrender uneventfully and making their destruction unnecessary. Gustav was later used in the Soviet Union at the siege of Sevastopol during Operation Barbarossa, with good effect, including destroying a munitions depot buried in the bedrock under a bay. Gustav was later captured by US troops and cut up, whilst Dora was destroyed near the end of the war to avoid capture by the Red Army.
